blocks.text: Lots and land in Vancouver Heights
Fee-simple lots

items.t: The sub-area's stock is detached houses on fee-simple lots — typical Burnaby residential lots, with larger and steeper view lots on the hill; Capitol Hill's upper streets are known for views over Burrard Inlet, downtown Vancouver and the North Shore mountains. A fee-simple Heights lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees — title, Burnaby bylaws and any registered covenants govern.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Vancouver Heights

items.t: What and where: Vancouver Heights is a City of Burnaby neighbourhood in northwest Burnaby (North Burnaby), on and below the Capitol Hill rise, with Hastings Street as its spine. The MLS® sub-area name (GVR board) is "Vancouver Heights." Nearby areas: Capitol Hill (the hilltop portion within/adjacent to this sub-area), Willingdon Heights, Parkcrest, Lochdale, Westridge, Burnaby Heights to the west, and the City of Vancouver (Hastings-Sunrise) across Boundary Road.

Plan frame: the City of Burnaby adopted the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan on December 9, 2025; it replaces the 1998 OCP Bylaw and takes precedence over older neighbourhood community-plan land use maps where they conflict. The Hastings Street corridor through the Heights is planned as the "Heights Urban Village," and the City has processed mixed-use redevelopment proposals on Hastings (for example at 4472 Hastings Street at Willingdon Avenue) to strengthen the village's urban fabric.

Over October 2025 – September 2026 the Burnaby detached median ranged $1,750,000 (June 2026) to $1,992,500 (December 2025); the condos & townhomes median ranged $643,250 (July 2026) to $720,000 (October 2025).

Housing fabric: predominantly detached single-family houses on a sloping, view-oriented hillside — early-to-mid 20th-century homes, post-war bungalows and Vancouver Special-era houses alongside newer custom rebuilds — with a limited number of low-rise apartments and condos along Hastings Street. Most homes are freehold; strata product is concentrated on or near Hastings.

Schools (SD41 Burnaby; Ministry-listed names only): two SD41 elementary schools sit on Pandora Street inside the sub-area — Confederation Park Elementary (4715 Pandora St, K–7) and Rosser Elementary (4375 Pandora St, K–7). Completed locator runs are documented on a single-address basis: 4375 Pandora St (locator range 4303–4375 PANDORA ST) → Rosser Elementary / Alpha Secondary (SD41 School Locator, run 2026-11-01), and the Capitol Hill sample 4715 Pandora St → Confederation Park Elementary / Alpha Secondary — so the two in-area Pandora Street elementaries split the street by address range while the secondary stays Alpha. Vancouver Heights catchment = Alpha Secondary on that settled chain. Catchments for other Heights addresses and school capacities: Not verified.

Transit: TransLink's R5 Hastings St RapidBus runs along Hastings Street through the Heights, linking Burrard Station in downtown Vancouver with SFU's Burnaby Mountain campus, at least every 10 minutes at peak and 15 minutes off-peak; in-area stops include Hythe, Holdom and Kensington. On September 7, 2026, TransLink extended the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station via Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue, serving Burnaby Heights with peak service every six to seven minutes and replacing the peak-only 222 bus. Published drive times to downtown Vancouver, Metrotown or SFU: Not verified.

Anchors: Confederation Park (250 Willingdon Avenue — one of Burnaby's largest parks, hosting the cenotaph for North Burnaby's Remembrance Day ceremony), the Eileen Dailly Leisure Pool & Fitness Centre (240 Willingdon Avenue), the McGill Branch of Burnaby Public Library (4595 Albert Street) and Capitol Hill Reservoir Park (229 N Hythe Avenue), a scenic viewpoint park at the top of Capitol Hill. A new Confederation Park Community Centre beside the pool and library is a City capital project whose replacement project has been deferred.

Flood / hazard: no area-wide flood construction level for the Capitol Hill slope was identified in the City sources read; parcel-level hazard or geotechnical status for individual Heights lots is not verified. No figure or zone is imported from any other area.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Vancouver Heights

items.t: City plans and zoning (Burnaby's own bylaws): the Burnaby 2050 OCP (adopted December 9, 2025) governs and takes precedence over older community-plan maps where they conflict; zoning is the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815, adopted June 9, 2026, in effect July 1, 2026) — never the former 1965 Bylaw No. 4742. Burnaby consolidated its former single- and two-family districts into one R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) District in June 2024: R1 lots may hold 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified.

Pricing the multiplex test: under R1, two otherwise similar Heights houses can be worth very different amounts to builders depending on lot area and the 400 m transit test (the R5/R2 Hastings corridor makes that test live on many lots — 6 units only near frequent transit). For Hastings-fronting and near-Hastings properties, review the Burnaby 2050 OCP land use map and the Heights Urban Village direction before assuming redevelopment or assembly value, because the new OCP takes precedence over older community plan maps.
Older-stock diligence: Parcel-level flood, slope or geotechnical status: Not verified per lot.

No Vancouver Empty Homes Tax in Burnaby — the name trap, stated expressly: the EHT (3% of assessed value) is a City of Vancouver tax and does not apply in Vancouver Heights, because Vancouver Heights is in Burnaby. The provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax is its own regime and is not the EHT.

blocks.text: Good to know about Vancouver Heights

items.t: Two near-identical building names sit five blocks apart on the same street. Confirm the street address, not just the name, before booking a showing.
The "Heights" brand crosses the sub-area line. A Heights buyer's comparable set changes depending on which side of the filing line a building sits.

The civic cluster is mid-replacement — and deferred. The new Confederation Park Community Centre would retain the McGill Branch library (built 2001) and Eileen Dailly pool (built 1992) and replace the 1971 seniors centre — but the City states the replacement project has been deferred, so the 1971-vintage centre remains the operating fact.

The park is also the war memorial. Confederation Park hosts the cenotaph where North Burnaby's Remembrance Day ceremony is held — the sub-area's civic anchor is a park, a pool, a library and a memorial in one cluster at Willingdon and Albert.

Childcare arrived by repurposing a school. In August 2026 the Province announced funding to repurpose school space at Confederation Park Elementary for 20 new before- and after-school child care spaces — an in-area school gaining a second use, on a street whose two elementaries split the catchment.

The view is the lot, street by street. Capitol Hill's upper streets are known for views over Burrard Inlet, downtown Vancouver and the North Shore mountains, and view premium and sun exposure change street by street on the slope — with detached turnover at 38% in September 2026, pricing the view correctly is the whole game on the hill.

Zero townhome complexes and zero bare-land strata is a verified finding, not a missing search. The Heights' ground-oriented supply is the detached house — which is why its R1 multiplex potential, not a townhouse complex or a lot package, is the ground-oriented conversation here.

blocks.text: Vancouver Heights home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

19 houses sold in Vancouver Heights with a median price of $2,075,000 (the middle half sold between $1,665,000 and $2,221,500), taking a median of 21 days to sell at 97.1% of the last list price; 11% sold above list. They had a median $770 per square foot, a median year built of 1978 and a median lot of 4,049 square feet. 15 condos sold in Vancouver Heights with a median price of $565,000 (the middle half sold between $491,500 and $976,900), taking a median of 26 days to sell at 95.9% of the last list price; 7% sold above list. They had a median $790 per square foot, a median year built of 2006 and a median strata fee of $397 a month.

faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 10 houses and 24 condos and townhomes listed in Vancouver Heights. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.
faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Vancouver Heights?

faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 40% (a sellers’ market); condos and townhomes had 8% (a buyers’ market). The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.
faq.q: Is Vancouver Heights a buyers’ or sellers’ market?

faq.a: 15 houses and 9 condos and townhomes sold in Vancouver Heights over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in September with 5 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in July with 3 sold.
faq.q: How many homes sold in Vancouver Heights from June to October 2026?

faq.a: In October 2026, Vancouver Heights held 2.3% of the 430 detached houses listed in Burnaby and 1.8% of the 1,309 condos and townhomes listed in Burnaby.
faq.q: How big is Vancouver Heights compared with the rest of Burnaby?

faq.a: In October 2026, houses made up 29.4% of the 34 homes listed in Vancouver Heights and condos and townhomes made up 70.6%; of the 6 that sold, houses were 66.7% and condos and townhomes 33.3%.
faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Vancouver Heights?

faq.a: Listings of detached houses fell from 16 in June to 10 in October 2026 (−37.5%); condos and townhomes rose from 16 in June to 24 in October 2026 (+50.0%).
faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Vancouver Heights than in June?

faq.a: No — Burnaby. Despite the name, Vancouver Heights is a City of Burnaby neighbourhood in North Burnaby, east of Boundary Road; its market statistics are reported under Burnaby in the SnapStats GVR report, and Burnaby's taxes, bylaws and school district (SD41) apply — including no Vancouver Empty Homes Tax.

No named bare-land subdivision and no bare-land strata community is verified here. What trades is the fee-simple hillside house lot — and its R1 multiplex potential. If a listing suggests strata tenure on a detached-looking lot, tenure is a title check, not a listing-field check.
faq.q: Is there a bare-land subdivision or a strata lot I can buy in the Heights?

faq.a: Under the R1 SSMUH District, most Heights lots allow 3–6 homes — 6 only within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop on a lot of at least 281 m² — and multi-unit product may be stratified, so lot area and the transit test can make two similar houses worth very different amounts to builders. Price the multiplex value before listing as a teardown, and check the Burnaby 2050 OCP / Heights Urban Village direction for Hastings-fronting lots.
faq.q: What is my Hastings house lot worth as a multiplex site?

faq.a: Yes, where the district's conditions are met — Burnaby's R1 district provides that lots with two or more primary units may be stratified. The resulting units are strata lots: Form B diligence, fees and bylaws apply to each.
faq.q: Can a multiplex built on a Heights lot be sold unit by unit?

faq.a: Alpha Secondary, on the settled SD41 locator chain: the run for 4375 Pandora St returned Rosser Elementary / Alpha Secondary, and the Capitol Hill sample on the same street (4715 Pandora St) also returned Alpha Secondary. Burnaby North Secondary is located in North Burnaby but is not the catchment secondary for those Pandora addresses. Other addresses: Not verified — run the specific address.
faq.q: Which secondary school serves the Heights — Alpha or Burnaby North?
What did houses in Vancouver Heights sell for?
faq.a: 19 houses sold in Vancouver Heights between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $2,075,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Vancouver Heights?
faq.a: The median was 21 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.1% of the last list price (11% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
